name: What should I move first in a bathroom remodel: plumbing or layout design?

mainEntity.name: What should I move first in a bathroom remodel: plumbing or layout design?
mainEntity.text: What should I move first in a bathroom remodel: plumbing or layout design?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bathroom layout design should come before plumbing relocation. The plumbing is the hidden infrastructure that supports the final room plan, so fixture placement, clearances, door swings, storage, and circulation should be decided first. Once the layout is locked, the contractor can determine whether the toilet, shower, vanity, or tub can stay near existing lines or needs to move. This sequence prevents expensive changes after demolition and reduces the risk of rough-in errors. It also helps align plumbing with tile layout, waterproofing, and cabinetry details. In high-end remodels, the biggest mistakes often happen when the plumbing is moved before the design is fully settled. Homeowners should ask for a coordinated plan that shows fixture positions, pipe routes, and finish dimensions together. That way the plumbing work supports the design instead of limiting it.
